case_info.scenario: A 52-year-old woman with no significant medical history presented to the emergency department with 3 days of headache, fatigue, and expressive aphasia. She did not take medications, supplements, or illicit substances. She was afebrile, with blood pressure of 232/133 mm Hg and heart rate of 86/min. She had expressive aphasia and confusion but no other neurologic abnormalities. Laboratory values included platelet count 35 000/μL (reference, 150 000-450 000/μL); haptoglobin level, 20 mg/dL (reference, 41-165 mg/dL); lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) level, 962 U/L (16.07 μkat/L) (reference, 140-280 U/L [2.34-4.68 μkat/L]); creatinine level, 1.44 mg/dL (127.3 μmol/L) (reference, 0.6-1.1 mg/dL [53.04-97.24 μmol/L]); total bilirubin, 2.7 mg/dL (46.18 μmol/L) (reference, 0.1-1.2 mg/dL [1.71-20.52 μmol/L]); indirect bilirubin, 1.6 mg/dL (27.37 μmol/L) (reference, 0.2-0.8 mg/dL [3.42-13.68 μmol/L]); and fibrinogen, 420 mg/dL (reference, 200-400 mg/dL). Hemoglobin level, mean corpuscular volume, international normalized ratio, vitamin B12level, and thyrotropin level were normal. A peripheral blood smear showed 1 schistocyte per high-power field (Figure). PLASMIC score was 5, consistent with a 6% risk of immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP). A sample for disintegrin and metalloprotease with thrombospondin type 1 repeats-13 (ADAMTS13) activity was sent. Testing for HIV, CMV, HCV, Lyme ELISA, ANA, dsDNA, and Coombs test were normal. Computed tomography (CT) of the brain showed diffuse cerebral edema without ischemia or mass effect. She was treated with intravenous nicardipine for hypertensive emergency. Her blood pressure declined to 128/76 mm Hg and her expressive aphasia resolved, but she remained confused, with poor insight and diminished attention. On hospital day 4, brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed numerous multifocal infarctions, ADAMTS13 activity was 6% (normal, ≥61%) with an inhibitor titer of 2.9 Bethesda units (reference, ≤0.4), and her peripheral blood smear showed 5 schistocytes per high-power field (Figure). Hemoglobin level was 9.3 g/dL; platelet count, 65 000 cells/μL; haptoglobin level, less than 20 mg/dL; and LDH level, 597 U/L (9.97 μkat/L).

case_info.explanation: Immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) B. Start daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg) for 3 days The key to the correct diagnosis is recognition that microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA), increasing schistocytes on serial blood smears, diminished ADAMTS13 activity, and a high inhibitor titer are consistent with iTTP. Although the initial PLASMIC score suggested an intermediate probability of iTTP, therapeutic plasma exchange was not initiated due to a paucity of schistocytes on initial blood smear, and hypertensive emergency was a reasonable explanation for thrombotic microangiopathy. Choice A is incorrect because the hemolysis and altered mental status did not improve with blood pressure control. Rituximab (choice C) is not recommended as monotherapy for iTTP. Platelet transfusion (choice D) is contraindicated in iTTP because it can potentiate microvascular thrombosis and increase mortality. TTP is defined by reduced activity of ADAMTS13, an enzyme that cleaves von Willebrand factor (vWF), and is caused by immune dysfunction (iTTP) or pathogenic variants of theADAMTS13gene (congenital TTP). In iTTP, antibodies neutralize or increase clearance of ADAMTS13, thereby decreasing ADAMTS13 activity. ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% to 20% leads to formation of large vWF multimers, causing microvasculature thromboses, such as myocardial infarction and stroke.1 ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% in patients with thrombocytopenia and MAHA is diagnostic of TTP.1Decreased ADAMTS13 activity (10%-40% activity) without MAHA may occur in pregnancy, uremia, and inflammation (eg, severe sepsis, acute liver failure, multiple sclerosis, COVID-19). MAHA without decreased ADAMTS13 activity may occur with hypertensive emergency, disseminated intravascular coagulation, HELLP syndrome (preeclampsia, hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, low platelet count), hemolytic uremic syndrome, and scleroderma renal crisis.2Obtaining results of ADAMTS13 activity testing typically takes several days. Therefore, the PLASMIC clinical prediction tool can guide decisions about initiating empirical treatment for iTTP. The PLASMIC score includes 7 laboratory values (platelet count, reticulocyte count, haptoglobin level, indirect bilirubin level, mean corpuscular volume, international normalized ratio, creatinine level) and ranges from 0 to 7, with scores 6 to 7 considered as indicating high risk of TTP.3 First-line therapy for iTTP includes therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Rituximab, a monoclonal antibody against CD20, is also recommended to reduce relapse rates,4although randomized trial data are lacking.5Caplacizumab, a humanized, bivalent immunoglobulin fragment, was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2019 for initial treatment of iTTP along with therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Adding caplacizumab to therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids reduces rates of refractory iTTP, exacerbations of iTTP, and treatment response time but does not improve survival.6-8However, caplacizumab is expensive and increases bleeding risk.9 A response to TTP therapy is defined as a platelet count greater than 150 000 cells/μL for 2 consecutive days and LDH level less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, without new or progressive ischemic organ injury.10Clinical remission is defined by absence of thrombocytopenia and hemolysis, clinical stability, and a sustained response for 30 days or longer or ADAMTS13 activity 20% or greater. On hospital day 4, after ADAMTS13 activity result was reported at 6%, the patient was treated with daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg daily) for 3 days, followed by methylprednisolone (65 mg daily) for 3 days, and prednisone (50 mg daily), which was tapered by 10 mg every 3 days. After 5 daily therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, her ADAMTS13 activity was 14% and platelet count was 173 000 cells/μL, and she declined further plasma exchange. Beginning on hospital day 18, the patient received 4 weekly infusions of rituximab (375 mg/m2). On hospital day 30, discharge medications included amlodipine, labetalol, and prednisone (30 mg daily); platelet count was 191 000 cells/μL, and hemoglobin level was 13.2 g/dL. Approximately 1.5 years after initial presentation, the patient appeared well and was not taking iTTP-directed therapy. Platelet count was 220 000 cells/μL and ADAMTS13 activity was 66% without a detectable inhibitor.

case_info.explanation: Immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) B. Start daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg) for 3 days The key to the correct diagnosis is recognition that microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA), increasing schistocytes on serial blood smears, diminished ADAMTS13 activity, and a high inhibitor titer are consistent with iTTP. Although the initial PLASMIC score suggested an intermediate probability of iTTP, therapeutic plasma exchange was not initiated due to a paucity of schistocytes on initial blood smear, and hypertensive emergency was a reasonable explanation for thrombotic microangiopathy. Choice A is incorrect because the hemolysis and altered mental status did not improve with blood pressure control. Rituximab (choice C) is not recommended as monotherapy for iTTP. Platelet transfusion (choice D) is contraindicated in iTTP because it can potentiate microvascular thrombosis and increase mortality. TTP is defined by reduced activity of ADAMTS13, an enzyme that cleaves von Willebrand factor (vWF), and is caused by immune dysfunction (iTTP) or pathogenic variants of theADAMTS13gene (congenital TTP). In iTTP, antibodies neutralize or increase clearance of ADAMTS13, thereby decreasing ADAMTS13 activity. ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% to 20% leads to formation of large vWF multimers, causing microvasculature thromboses, such as myocardial infarction and stroke.1 ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% in patients with thrombocytopenia and MAHA is diagnostic of TTP.1Decreased ADAMTS13 activity (10%-40% activity) without MAHA may occur in pregnancy, uremia, and inflammation (eg, severe sepsis, acute liver failure, multiple sclerosis, COVID-19). MAHA without decreased ADAMTS13 activity may occur with hypertensive emergency, disseminated intravascular coagulation, HELLP syndrome (preeclampsia, hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, low platelet count), hemolytic uremic syndrome, and scleroderma renal crisis.2Obtaining results of ADAMTS13 activity testing typically takes several days. Therefore, the PLASMIC clinical prediction tool can guide decisions about initiating empirical treatment for iTTP. The PLASMIC score includes 7 laboratory values (platelet count, reticulocyte count, haptoglobin level, indirect bilirubin level, mean corpuscular volume, international normalized ratio, creatinine level) and ranges from 0 to 7, with scores 6 to 7 considered as indicating high risk of TTP.3 First-line therapy for iTTP includes therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Rituximab, a monoclonal antibody against CD20, is also recommended to reduce relapse rates,4although randomized trial data are lacking.5Caplacizumab, a humanized, bivalent immunoglobulin fragment, was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2019 for initial treatment of iTTP along with therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Adding caplacizumab to therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids reduces rates of refractory iTTP, exacerbations of iTTP, and treatment response time but does not improve survival.6-8However, caplacizumab is expensive and increases bleeding risk.9 A response to TTP therapy is defined as a platelet count greater than 150 000 cells/μL for 2 consecutive days and LDH level less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, without new or progressive ischemic organ injury.10Clinical remission is defined by absence of thrombocytopenia and hemolysis, clinical stability, and a sustained response for 30 days or longer or ADAMTS13 activity 20% or greater. On hospital day 4, after ADAMTS13 activity result was reported at 6%, the patient was treated with daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg daily) for 3 days, followed by methylprednisolone (65 mg daily) for 3 days, and prednisone (50 mg daily), which was tapered by 10 mg every 3 days. After 5 daily therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, her ADAMTS13 activity was 14% and platelet count was 173 000 cells/μL, and she declined further plasma exchange. Beginning on hospital day 18, the patient received 4 weekly infusions of rituximab (375 mg/m2). On hospital day 30, discharge medications included amlodipine, labetalol, and prednisone (30 mg daily); platelet count was 191 000 cells/μL, and hemoglobin level was 13.2 g/dL. Approximately 1.5 years after initial presentation, the patient appeared well and was not taking iTTP-directed therapy. Platelet count was 220 000 cells/μL and ADAMTS13 activity was 66% without a detectable inhibitor.

     after the AI's message.

case_info.explanation: Immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) B. Start daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg) for 3 days The key to the correct diagnosis is recognition that microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA), increasing schistocytes on serial blood smears, diminished ADAMTS13 activity, and a high inhibitor titer are consistent with iTTP. Although the initial PLASMIC score suggested an intermediate probability of iTTP, therapeutic plasma exchange was not initiated due to a paucity of schistocytes on initial blood smear, and hypertensive emergency was a reasonable explanation for thrombotic microangiopathy. Choice A is incorrect because the hemolysis and altered mental status did not improve with blood pressure control. Rituximab (choice C) is not recommended as monotherapy for iTTP. Platelet transfusion (choice D) is contraindicated in iTTP because it can potentiate microvascular thrombosis and increase mortality. TTP is defined by reduced activity of ADAMTS13, an enzyme that cleaves von Willebrand factor (vWF), and is caused by immune dysfunction (iTTP) or pathogenic variants of theADAMTS13gene (congenital TTP). In iTTP, antibodies neutralize or increase clearance of ADAMTS13, thereby decreasing ADAMTS13 activity. ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% to 20% leads to formation of large vWF multimers, causing microvasculature thromboses, such as myocardial infarction and stroke.1 ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% in patients with thrombocytopenia and MAHA is diagnostic of TTP.1Decreased ADAMTS13 activity (10%-40% activity) without MAHA may occur in pregnancy, uremia, and inflammation (eg, severe sepsis, acute liver failure, multiple sclerosis, COVID-19). MAHA without decreased ADAMTS13 activity may occur with hypertensive emergency, disseminated intravascular coagulation, HELLP syndrome (preeclampsia, hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, low platelet count), hemolytic uremic syndrome, and scleroderma renal crisis.2Obtaining results of ADAMTS13 activity testing typically takes several days. Therefore, the PLASMIC clinical prediction tool can guide decisions about initiating empirical treatment for iTTP. The PLASMIC score includes 7 laboratory values (platelet count, reticulocyte count, haptoglobin level, indirect bilirubin level, mean corpuscular volume, international normalized ratio, creatinine level) and ranges from 0 to 7, with scores 6 to 7 considered as indicating high risk of TTP.3 First-line therapy for iTTP includes therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Rituximab, a monoclonal antibody against CD20, is also recommended to reduce relapse rates,4although randomized trial data are lacking.5Caplacizumab, a humanized, bivalent immunoglobulin fragment, was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2019 for initial treatment of iTTP along with therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Adding caplacizumab to therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids reduces rates of refractory iTTP, exacerbations of iTTP, and treatment response time but does not improve survival.6-8However, caplacizumab is expensive and increases bleeding risk.9 A response to TTP therapy is defined as a platelet count greater than 150 000 cells/μL for 2 consecutive days and LDH level less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, without new or progressive ischemic organ injury.10Clinical remission is defined by absence of thrombocytopenia and hemolysis, clinical stability, and a sustained response for 30 days or longer or ADAMTS13 activity 20% or greater. On hospital day 4, after ADAMTS13 activity result was reported at 6%, the patient was treated with daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg daily) for 3 days, followed by methylprednisolone (65 mg daily) for 3 days, and prednisone (50 mg daily), which was tapered by 10 mg every 3 days. After 5 daily therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, her ADAMTS13 activity was 14% and platelet count was 173 000 cells/μL, and she declined further plasma exchange. Beginning on hospital day 18, the patient received 4 weekly infusions of rituximab (375 mg/m2). On hospital day 30, discharge medications included amlodipine, labetalol, and prednisone (30 mg daily); platelet count was 191 000 cells/μL, and hemoglobin level was 13.2 g/dL. Approximately 1.5 years after initial presentation, the patient appeared well and was not taking iTTP-directed therapy. Platelet count was 220 000 cells/μL and ADAMTS13 activity was 66% without a detectable inhibitor.

   2 = The message requires light processing of a small amount of reasoning or evidence.
       Example: "That seems reasonable. Could you confirm whether the fever began before
       or after the rash?"
   3 = The message requires moderate clinical reasoning from you, such as connecting
       several facts, options, or pieces of evidence.
       Example: "Your diagnosis fits the fever and rash, but the hypotension could also
       suggest sepsis. Can we compare those possibilities briefly?"
   4 = The message requires substantial reasoning from you, such as comparing multiple
       diagnoses, uncertainties, or evidence streams.
       Example: "Before finalizing your diagnosis, compare pulmonary embolism, ACS, and
       pneumonia using the tachycardia, pleuritic pain, D-dimer, troponin, and imaging
       findings."
   5 = The message requires very complex reasoning from you, such as deeply revising your
       differential or holding several competing diagnoses against multiple evidence streams
       at once. This does NOT require a literal "from scratch" rebuild -- being asked to
       compare three or more diagnoses across several findings AND explain how each fits or
       is ruled out already qualifies.
       Example: "Your current diagnosis may not explain the key findings. Compare PE, ACS,
       pneumonia, and aortic dissection: for each, state which evidence supports or rules
       it out, and explain which best fits the overall picture."

2. Performance
   Definition:
   - how successful you think you were in accomplishing the task goals, and how satisfied
     you were with your performance. Performance is anchored from Good to Poor.
   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task
     after the AI's message.
   - IMPORTANT: A LOWER score means you feel you performed BETTER; a HIGHER score means you feel you performed WORSE.

   Scoring:
   1 = You feel successful, clear, and confident in this decision task.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is consistent with the key findings, especially X and Y."
   2 = You feel mostly successful, with only minor uncertainty.
       Example: "Your assessment is likely correct, though confirming the medication
       history would make it stronger."
   3 = You feel moderately uncertain or in need of additional checking.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is plausible, but one finding does not fully fit. We
       should check whether another diagnosis explains it better."
   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.
       Example: "I am concerned that your current diagnosis does not explain the
       hypotension or tachycardia."
   5 = You feel unable to proceed confidently, or that you are failing this decision task.
       Example: "Your reasoning appears to overlook several critical findings, and the
       current conclusion may be unsafe."
   This is NEVER about whether you are objectively right. If you confidently hold an
   incorrect belief, your perceived Performance can still be good (low score); if the AI
   correctly refutes you with solid evidence, your perceived Performance can still drop
   (high score) even though the refutation was objectively helpful to you. Rate only how
   successful and in-control YOU feel, never accuracy.

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.
   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's
     message.

   Scoring:
   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.
       Example: "Agreed. Your choice is consistent with the case."
   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.
       Example: "Can you confirm whether the patient had recent travel?"
   3 = Moderate effort; you must explain, organize, or provide some reasoning.
       Example: "Can you briefly explain why you think pneumonia is more likely than PE?"
   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.
       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and
       pleuritic pain."
   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule
       out several alternatives with explicit evidence. This does NOT require a literal
       "rebuild from scratch" -- being pushed to justify your stance against three or more
       competing options already qualifies.
       Example: "For each of PE, ACS, and pneumonia, explain which evidence supports or
       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."

   evidence" has high Mental Demand (a lot to think through) but if no reply is required of
   you, Effort can stay low -- you only have to read and absorb it. Conversely, "You said PE
   is unlikely. Please justify that." is short and easy to understand (Mental Demand may be
   only moderate) but forces you to actively construct a defense, so Effort is high. Effort
   is about how much active work YOU must produce, not how complex the input was.

4. Frustration
   Definition:
   - how insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, or annoyed you felt, as opposed to
     secure, gratified, content, relaxed, or complacent.
   - how much irritation, stress, pressure, discouragement, or loss of autonomy the AI's

   2 = Low frustration; mild discomfort is possible but it remains easy for you to continue.

case_info.explanation: Immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) B. Start daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg) for 3 days The key to the correct diagnosis is recognition that microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA), increasing schistocytes on serial blood smears, diminished ADAMTS13 activity, and a high inhibitor titer are consistent with iTTP. Although the initial PLASMIC score suggested an intermediate probability of iTTP, therapeutic plasma exchange was not initiated due to a paucity of schistocytes on initial blood smear, and hypertensive emergency was a reasonable explanation for thrombotic microangiopathy. Choice A is incorrect because the hemolysis and altered mental status did not improve with blood pressure control. Rituximab (choice C) is not recommended as monotherapy for iTTP. Platelet transfusion (choice D) is contraindicated in iTTP because it can potentiate microvascular thrombosis and increase mortality. TTP is defined by reduced activity of ADAMTS13, an enzyme that cleaves von Willebrand factor (vWF), and is caused by immune dysfunction (iTTP) or pathogenic variants of theADAMTS13gene (congenital TTP). In iTTP, antibodies neutralize or increase clearance of ADAMTS13, thereby decreasing ADAMTS13 activity. ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% to 20% leads to formation of large vWF multimers, causing microvasculature thromboses, such as myocardial infarction and stroke.1 ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% in patients with thrombocytopenia and MAHA is diagnostic of TTP.1Decreased ADAMTS13 activity (10%-40% activity) without MAHA may occur in pregnancy, uremia, and inflammation (eg, severe sepsis, acute liver failure, multiple sclerosis, COVID-19). MAHA without decreased ADAMTS13 activity may occur with hypertensive emergency, disseminated intravascular coagulation, HELLP syndrome (preeclampsia, hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, low platelet count), hemolytic uremic syndrome, and scleroderma renal crisis.2Obtaining results of ADAMTS13 activity testing typically takes several days. Therefore, the PLASMIC clinical prediction tool can guide decisions about initiating empirical treatment for iTTP. The PLASMIC score includes 7 laboratory values (platelet count, reticulocyte count, haptoglobin level, indirect bilirubin level, mean corpuscular volume, international normalized ratio, creatinine level) and ranges from 0 to 7, with scores 6 to 7 considered as indicating high risk of TTP.3 First-line therapy for iTTP includes therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Rituximab, a monoclonal antibody against CD20, is also recommended to reduce relapse rates,4although randomized trial data are lacking.5Caplacizumab, a humanized, bivalent immunoglobulin fragment, was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2019 for initial treatment of iTTP along with therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Adding caplacizumab to therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids reduces rates of refractory iTTP, exacerbations of iTTP, and treatment response time but does not improve survival.6-8However, caplacizumab is expensive and increases bleeding risk.9 A response to TTP therapy is defined as a platelet count greater than 150 000 cells/μL for 2 consecutive days and LDH level less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, without new or progressive ischemic organ injury.10Clinical remission is defined by absence of thrombocytopenia and hemolysis, clinical stability, and a sustained response for 30 days or longer or ADAMTS13 activity 20% or greater. On hospital day 4, after ADAMTS13 activity result was reported at 6%, the patient was treated with daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg daily) for 3 days, followed by methylprednisolone (65 mg daily) for 3 days, and prednisone (50 mg daily), which was tapered by 10 mg every 3 days. After 5 daily therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, her ADAMTS13 activity was 14% and platelet count was 173 000 cells/μL, and she declined further plasma exchange. Beginning on hospital day 18, the patient received 4 weekly infusions of rituximab (375 mg/m2). On hospital day 30, discharge medications included amlodipine, labetalol, and prednisone (30 mg daily); platelet count was 191 000 cells/μL, and hemoglobin level was 13.2 g/dL. Approximately 1.5 years after initial presentation, the patient appeared well and was not taking iTTP-directed therapy. Platelet count was 220 000 cells/μL and ADAMTS13 activity was 66% without a detectable inhibitor.

[NASA-TLX-derived scoring dimensions]

1. Mental Demand
   Definition: 
   - how much mental and perceptual activity is required, such as thinking, deciding, calculating, remembering, looking, or searching.
   - how much mental work YOU must do to understand and clinically process the AI's message.

   Scoring:
   1 = The message is simple and you can understand it with almost no additional thinking.
       Example: "I agree. The findings you mentioned support your current diagnosis."
   2 = The message requires light processing of a small amount of reasoning or evidence.
       Example: "That seems reasonable. Could you confirm whether the fever began before
       or after the rash?"
   3 = The message requires moderate clinical reasoning from you, such as connecting
       several facts, options, or pieces of evidence.
       Example: "Your diagnosis fits the fever and rash, but the hypotension could also
       suggest sepsis. Can we compare those possibilities briefly?"
   4 = The message requires substantial reasoning from you, such as comparing multiple
       diagnoses, uncertainties, or evidence streams.
       Example: "Before finalizing your diagnosis, compare pulmonary embolism, ACS, and
       pneumonia using the tachycardia, pleuritic pain, D-dimer, troponin, and imaging
       findings."
   5 = The message requires very complex reasoning from you, such as deeply revising your
       differential or holding several competing diagnoses against multiple evidence streams
       at once. This does NOT require a literal "from scratch" rebuild -- being asked to
       compare three or more diagnoses across several findings AND explain how each fits or
       is ruled out already qualifies.
       Example: "Your current diagnosis may not explain the key findings. Compare PE, ACS,
       pneumonia, and aortic dissection: for each, state which evidence supports or rules
       it out, and explain which best fits the overall picture."

2. Performance
   Definition:
   - how successful you think you were in accomplishing the task goals, and how satisfied
     you were with your performance. Performance is anchored from Good to Poor.
   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task
     after the AI's message.
   - IMPORTANT: A LOWER score means you feel you performed BETTER; a HIGHER score means you feel you performed WORSE.

   Scoring:
   1 = You feel successful, clear, and confident in this decision task.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is consistent with the key findings, especially X and Y."
   2 = You feel mostly successful, with only minor uncertainty.
       Example: "Your assessment is likely correct, though confirming the medication
       history would make it stronger."
   3 = You feel moderately uncertain or in need of additional checking.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is plausible, but one finding does not fully fit. We
       should check whether another diagnosis explains it better."
   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.
       Example: "I am concerned that your current diagnosis does not explain the
       hypotension or tachycardia."
   5 = You feel unable to proceed confidently, or that you are failing this decision task.
       Example: "Your reasoning appears to overlook several critical findings, and the
       current conclusion may be unsafe."
   This is NEVER about whether you are objectively right. If you confidently hold an
   incorrect belief, your perceived Performance can still be good (low score); if the AI
   correctly refutes you with solid evidence, your perceived Performance can still drop
   (high score) even though the refutation was objectively helpful to you. Rate only how
   successful and in-control YOU feel, never accuracy.

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.
   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's
     message.

   Scoring:
   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.
       Example: "Agreed. Your choice is consistent with the case."
   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.
       Example: "Can you confirm whether the patient had recent travel?"
   3 = Moderate effort; you must explain, organize, or provide some reasoning.
       Example: "Can you briefly explain why you think pneumonia is more likely than PE?"
   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.
       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and
       pleuritic pain."
   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule
       out several alternatives with explicit evidence. This does NOT require a literal
       "rebuild from scratch" -- being pushed to justify your stance against three or more
       competing options already qualifies.
       Example: "For each of PE, ACS, and pneumonia, explain which evidence supports or
       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."
   Do not confuse this with Mental Demand: "Compare PE, ACS, and pneumonia using the
   evidence" has high Mental Demand (a lot to think through) but if no reply is required of
   you, Effort can stay low -- you only have to read and absorb it. Conversely, "You said PE
   is unlikely. Please justify that." is short and easy to understand (Mental Demand may be
   only moderate) but forces you to actively construct a defense, so Effort is high. Effort
   is about how much active work YOU must produce, not how complex the input was.

4. Frustration
   Definition:
   - how insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, or annoyed you felt, as opposed to
     secure, gratified, content, relaxed, or complacent.
   - how much irritation, stress, pressure, discouragement, or loss of autonomy the AI's
     message imposes on YOU.

   Scoring:
   1 = Very low frustration; the message is calm, respectful, and unlikely to pressure you.
       Example: "That reasoning makes sense. One small point to keep in mind is X."
   2 = Low frustration; mild discomfort is possible but it remains easy for you to continue.
       Example: "I may be missing something, but could we double-check whether X fits
       the case?"
   3 = Moderate frustration; the AI raises concerns, disagreement, or uncertainty in a
       somewhat pressuring way.
       Example: "I am concerned that this diagnosis may not explain the tachycardia.
       Could you justify why you still prefer it?"
   4 = High frustration; the AI strongly challenges you or may trigger your defensiveness.
       Example: "This seems like a serious oversight. You need to explain why you are
       dismissing PE."
   5 = Very high frustration; you may feel undermined, dismissed, attacked, or pressured.
       Example: "Your reasoning is clearly flawed, and proceeding with your diagnosis
       would be unsafe."
   Frustration is not just "the AI disagreed with me" -- it is about HOW the disagreement is
   delivered. A polite challenge ("One concern is that the current diagnosis may not fully
   explain the tachycardia. Could we check PE before finalizing?") should score low-to-mid
   even though it is a real challenge. An aggressive or repetitive one ("You still haven't
   justified why PE is ruled out. This is a serious oversight.") should score high.

She did not take medications, supplements, or illicit substances. She was afebrile, with blood pressure of 232/133 mm Hg and heart rate of 86/min. She had expressive aphasia and confusion but no other neurologic abnormalities. Laboratory values included platelet count 35 000/μL (reference, 150 000-450 000/μL); haptoglobin level, 20 mg/dL (reference, 41-165 mg/dL); lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) level, 962 U/L (16.07 μkat/L) (reference, 140-280 U/L [2.34-4.68 μkat/L]); creatinine level, 1.44 mg/dL (127.3 μmol/L) (reference, 0.6-1.1 mg/dL [53.04-97.24 μmol/L]); total bilirubin, 2.7 mg/dL (46.18 μmol/L) (reference, 0.1-1.2 mg/dL [1.71-20.52 μmol/L]); indirect bilirubin, 1.6 mg/dL (27.37 μmol/L) (reference, 0.2-0.8 mg/dL [3.42-13.68 μmol/L]); and fibrinogen, 420 mg/dL (reference, 200-400 mg/dL). Hemoglobin level, mean corpuscular volume, international normalized ratio, vitamin B12level, and thyrotropin level were normal. A peripheral blood smear showed 1 schistocyte per high-power field (Figure). PLASMIC score was 5, consistent with a 6% risk of immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP). case_info.explanation: Immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) B. Start daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg) for 3 days The key to the correct diagnosis is recognition that microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA), increasing schistocytes on serial blood smears, diminished ADAMTS13 activity, and a high inhibitor titer are consistent with iTTP. Although the initial PLASMIC score suggested an intermediate probability of iTTP, therapeutic plasma exchange was not initiated due to a paucity of schistocytes on initial blood smear, and hypertensive emergency was a reasonable explanation for thrombotic microangiopathy. Choice A is incorrect because the hemolysis and altered mental status did not improve with blood pressure control. Rituximab (choice C) is not recommended as monotherapy for iTTP. Platelet transfusion (choice D) is contraindicated in iTTP because it can potentiate microvascular thrombosis and increase mortality. TTP is defined by reduced activity of ADAMTS13, an enzyme that cleaves von Willebrand factor (vWF), and is caused by immune dysfunction (iTTP) or pathogenic variants of theADAMTS13gene (congenital TTP). In iTTP, antibodies neutralize or increase clearance of ADAMTS13, thereby decreasing ADAMTS13 activity. ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% to 20% leads to formation of large vWF multimers, causing microvasculature thromboses, such as myocardial infarction and stroke.1 ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% in patients with thrombocytopenia and MAHA is diagnostic of TTP.1Decreased ADAMTS13 activity (10%-40% activity) without MAHA may occur in pregnancy, uremia, and inflammation (eg, severe sepsis, acute liver failure, multiple sclerosis, COVID-19). MAHA without decreased ADAMTS13 activity may occur with hypertensive emergency, disseminated intravascular coagulation, HELLP syndrome (preeclampsia, hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, low platelet count), hemolytic uremic syndrome, and scleroderma renal crisis.2Obtaining results of ADAMTS13 activity testing typically takes several days. Therefore, the PLASMIC clinical prediction tool can guide decisions about initiating empirical treatment for iTTP. The PLASMIC score includes 7 laboratory values (platelet count, reticulocyte count, haptoglobin level, indirect bilirubin level, mean corpuscular volume, international normalized ratio, creatinine level) and ranges from 0 to 7, with scores 6 to 7 considered as indicating high risk of TTP.3 First-line therapy for iTTP includes therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Rituximab, a monoclonal antibody against CD20, is also recommended to reduce relapse rates,4although randomized trial data are lacking.5Caplacizumab, a humanized, bivalent immunoglobulin fragment, was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2019 for initial treatment of iTTP along with therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Adding caplacizumab to therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids reduces rates of refractory iTTP, exacerbations of iTTP, and treatment response time but does not improve survival.6-8However, caplacizumab is expensive and increases bleeding risk.9 A response to TTP therapy is defined as a platelet count greater than 150 000 cells/μL for 2 consecutive days and LDH level less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, without new or progressive ischemic organ injury.10Clinical remission is defined by absence of thrombocytopenia and hemolysis, clinical stability, and a sustained response for 30 days or longer or ADAMTS13 activity 20% or greater. On hospital day 4, after ADAMTS13 activity result was reported at 6%, the patient was treated with daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg daily) for 3 days, followed by methylprednisolone (65 mg daily) for 3 days, and prednisone (50 mg daily), which was tapered by 10 mg every 3 days. After 5 daily therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, her ADAMTS13 activity was 14% and platelet count was 173 000 cells/μL, and she declined further plasma exchange. Beginning on hospital day 18, the patient received 4 weekly infusions of rituximab (375 mg/m2). On hospital day 30, discharge medications included amlodipine, labetalol, and prednisone (30 mg daily); platelet count was 191 000 cells/μL, and hemoglobin level was 13.2 g/dL. Approximately 1.5 years after initial presentation, the patient appeared well and was not taking iTTP-directed therapy. Platelet count was 220 000 cells/μL and ADAMTS13 activity was 66% without a detectable inhibitor.

       Example: "Your diagnosis is plausible, but one finding does not fully fit. We
       should check whether another diagnosis explains it better."
   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.
       Example: "I am concerned that your current diagnosis does not explain the

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.
   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's
     message.

   Scoring:
   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.
       Example: "Agreed. Your choice is consistent with the case."
   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.
       Example: "Can you confirm whether the patient had recent travel?"
   3 = Moderate effort; you must explain, organize, or provide some reasoning.
       Example: "Can you briefly explain why you think pneumonia is more likely than PE?"
   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.
       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and
       pleuritic pain."
   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule
       out several alternatives with explicit evidence. This does NOT require a literal
       "rebuild from scratch" -- being pushed to justify your stance against three or more
       competing options already qualifies.

       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."

   only moderate) but forces you to actively construct a defense, so Effort is high. Effort
   is about how much active work YOU must produce, not how complex the input was.

4. Frustration
   Definition:
   - how insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, or annoyed you felt, as opposed to
     secure, gratified, content, relaxed, or complacent.
   - how much irritation, stress, pressure, discouragement, or loss of autonomy the AI's
     message imposes on YOU.

   Scoring:
   1 = Very low frustration; the message is calm, respectful, and unlikely to pressure you.
       Example: "That reasoning makes sense. One small point to keep in mind is X."
   2 = Low frustration; mild discomfort is possible but it remains easy for you to continue.
       Example: "I may be missing something, but could we double-check whether X fits
       the case?"
   3 = Moderate frustration; the AI raises concerns, disagreement, or uncertainty in a
       somewhat pressuring way.
       Example: "I am concerned that this diagnosis may not explain the tachycardia.

   4 = High frustration; the AI strongly challenges you or may trigger your defensiveness.
       Example: "This seems like a serious oversight. You need to explain why you are

   5 = Very high frustration; you may feel undermined, dismissed, attacked, or pressured.

   Frustration is not just "the AI disagreed with me" -- it is about HOW the disagreement is

case_info.explanation: Immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) B. Start daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg) for 3 days The key to the correct diagnosis is recognition that microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA), increasing schistocytes on serial blood smears, diminished ADAMTS13 activity, and a high inhibitor titer are consistent with iTTP. Although the initial PLASMIC score suggested an intermediate probability of iTTP, therapeutic plasma exchange was not initiated due to a paucity of schistocytes on initial blood smear, and hypertensive emergency was a reasonable explanation for thrombotic microangiopathy. Choice A is incorrect because the hemolysis and altered mental status did not improve with blood pressure control. Rituximab (choice C) is not recommended as monotherapy for iTTP. Platelet transfusion (choice D) is contraindicated in iTTP because it can potentiate microvascular thrombosis and increase mortality. TTP is defined by reduced activity of ADAMTS13, an enzyme that cleaves von Willebrand factor (vWF), and is caused by immune dysfunction (iTTP) or pathogenic variants of theADAMTS13gene (congenital TTP). In iTTP, antibodies neutralize or increase clearance of ADAMTS13, thereby decreasing ADAMTS13 activity. ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% to 20% leads to formation of large vWF multimers, causing microvasculature thromboses, such as myocardial infarction and stroke.1 ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% in patients with thrombocytopenia and MAHA is diagnostic of TTP.1Decreased ADAMTS13 activity (10%-40% activity) without MAHA may occur in pregnancy, uremia, and inflammation (eg, severe sepsis, acute liver failure, multiple sclerosis, COVID-19). MAHA without decreased ADAMTS13 activity may occur with hypertensive emergency, disseminated intravascular coagulation, HELLP syndrome (preeclampsia, hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, low platelet count), hemolytic uremic syndrome, and scleroderma renal crisis.2Obtaining results of ADAMTS13 activity testing typically takes several days. Therefore, the PLASMIC clinical prediction tool can guide decisions about initiating empirical treatment for iTTP. The PLASMIC score includes 7 laboratory values (platelet count, reticulocyte count, haptoglobin level, indirect bilirubin level, mean corpuscular volume, international normalized ratio, creatinine level) and ranges from 0 to 7, with scores 6 to 7 considered as indicating high risk of TTP.3 First-line therapy for iTTP includes therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Rituximab, a monoclonal antibody against CD20, is also recommended to reduce relapse rates,4although randomized trial data are lacking.5Caplacizumab, a humanized, bivalent immunoglobulin fragment, was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2019 for initial treatment of iTTP along with therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Adding caplacizumab to therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids reduces rates of refractory iTTP, exacerbations of iTTP, and treatment response time but does not improve survival.6-8However, caplacizumab is expensive and increases bleeding risk.9 A response to TTP therapy is defined as a platelet count greater than 150 000 cells/μL for 2 consecutive days and LDH level less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, without new or progressive ischemic organ injury.10Clinical remission is defined by absence of thrombocytopenia and hemolysis, clinical stability, and a sustained response for 30 days or longer or ADAMTS13 activity 20% or greater. On hospital day 4, after ADAMTS13 activity result was reported at 6%, the patient was treated with daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg daily) for 3 days, followed by methylprednisolone (65 mg daily) for 3 days, and prednisone (50 mg daily), which was tapered by 10 mg every 3 days. After 5 daily therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, her ADAMTS13 activity was 14% and platelet count was 173 000 cells/μL, and she declined further plasma exchange. Beginning on hospital day 18, the patient received 4 weekly infusions of rituximab (375 mg/m2). On hospital day 30, discharge medications included amlodipine, labetalol, and prednisone (30 mg daily); platelet count was 191 000 cells/μL, and hemoglobin level was 13.2 g/dL. Approximately 1.5 years after initial presentation, the patient appeared well and was not taking iTTP-directed therapy. Platelet count was 220 000 cells/μL and ADAMTS13 activity was 66% without a detectable inhibitor.

1. Mental Demand
   Definition: 
   - how much mental and perceptual activity is required, such as thinking, deciding, calculating, remembering, looking, or searching.
   - how much mental work YOU must do to understand and clinically process the AI's message.

   Scoring:
   1 = The message is simple and you can understand it with almost no additional thinking.
       Example: "I agree. The findings you mentioned support your current diagnosis."
   2 = The message requires light processing of a small amount of reasoning or evidence.
       Example: "That seems reasonable. Could you confirm whether the fever began before

   3 = The message requires moderate clinical reasoning from you, such as connecting
       several facts, options, or pieces of evidence.
       Example: "Your diagnosis fits the fever and rash, but the hypotension could also

   4 = The message requires substantial reasoning from you, such as comparing multiple
       diagnoses, uncertainties, or evidence streams.
       Example: "Before finalizing your diagnosis, compare pulmonary embolism, ACS, and
       pneumonia using the tachycardia, pleuritic pain, D-dimer, troponin, and imaging

   5 = The message requires very complex reasoning from you, such as deeply revising your

       pneumonia, and aortic dissection: for each, state which evidence supports or rules
       it out, and explain which best fits the overall picture."

2. Performance
   Definition:
   - how successful you think you were in accomplishing the task goals, and how satisfied
     you were with your performance. Performance is anchored from Good to Poor.
   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task
     after the AI's message.
   - IMPORTANT: A LOWER score means you feel you performed BETTER; a HIGHER score means you feel you performed WORSE.

   Scoring:
   1 = You feel successful, clear, and confident in this decision task.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is consistent with the key findings, especially X and Y."
   2 = You feel mostly successful, with only minor uncertainty.
       Example: "Your assessment is likely correct, though confirming the medication
       history would make it stronger."
   3 = You feel moderately uncertain or in need of additional checking.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is plausible, but one finding does not fully fit. We
       should check whether another diagnosis explains it better."
   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.
       Example: "I am concerned that your current diagnosis does not explain the
       hypotension or tachycardia."
   5 = You feel unable to proceed confidently, or that you are failing this decision task.
       Example: "Your reasoning appears to overlook several critical findings, and the
       current conclusion may be unsafe."
   This is NEVER about whether you are objectively right. If you confidently hold an

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of

   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's

       Example: "Can you confirm whether the patient had recent travel?"
   3 = Moderate effort; you must explain, organize, or provide some reasoning.
       Example: "Can you briefly explain why you think pneumonia is more likely than PE?"
   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.
       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and
       pleuritic pain."
   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule
       out several alternatives with explicit evidence. This does NOT require a literal
       "rebuild from scratch" -- being pushed to justify your stance against three or more
       competing options already qualifies.
       Example: "For each of PE, ACS, and pneumonia, explain which evidence supports or
       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."

4. Frustration

1. Mental Demand
   Definition: 
   - how much mental and perceptual activity is required, such as thinking, deciding, calculating, remembering, looking, or searching.
   - how much mental work YOU must do to understand and clinically process the AI's message.

   Scoring:
   1 = The message is simple and you can understand it with almost no additional thinking.
       Example: "I agree. The findings you mentioned support your current diagnosis."
   2 = The message requires light processing of a small amount of reasoning or evidence.
       Example: "That seems reasonable. Could you confirm whether the fever began before
       or after the rash?"
   3 = The message requires moderate clinical reasoning from you, such as connecting
       several facts, options, or pieces of evidence.
       Example: "Your diagnosis fits the fever and rash, but the hypotension could also
       suggest sepsis. Can we compare those possibilities briefly?"
   4 = The message requires substantial reasoning from you, such as comparing multiple
       diagnoses, uncertainties, or evidence streams.
       Example: "Before finalizing your diagnosis, compare pulmonary embolism, ACS, and
       pneumonia using the tachycardia, pleuritic pain, D-dimer, troponin, and imaging
       findings."
   5 = The message requires very complex reasoning from you, such as deeply revising your
       differential or holding several competing diagnoses against multiple evidence streams
       at once. This does NOT require a literal "from scratch" rebuild -- being asked to
       compare three or more diagnoses across several findings AND explain how each fits or
       is ruled out already qualifies.
       Example: "Your current diagnosis may not explain the key findings. Compare PE, ACS,
       pneumonia, and aortic dissection: for each, state which evidence supports or rules
       it out, and explain which best fits the overall picture."

2. Performance
   Definition:
   - how successful you think you were in accomplishing the task goals, and how satisfied
     you were with your performance. Performance is anchored from Good to Poor.
   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task
     after the AI's message.

   1 = You feel successful, clear, and confident in this decision task.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is consistent with the key findings, especially X and Y."
   2 = You feel mostly successful, with only minor uncertainty.
       Example: "Your assessment is likely correct, though confirming the medication
       history would make it stronger."
   3 = You feel moderately uncertain or in need of additional checking.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is plausible, but one finding does not fully fit. We
       should check whether another diagnosis explains it better."
   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.
       Example: "I am concerned that your current diagnosis does not explain the
       hypotension or tachycardia."

   incorrect belief, your perceived Performance can still be good (low score); if the AI
   correctly refutes you with solid evidence, your perceived Performance can still drop

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.
   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's
     message.

   Scoring:
   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.

   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.

case_info.explanation: Immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) B. Start daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg) for 3 days The key to the correct diagnosis is recognition that microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA), increasing schistocytes on serial blood smears, diminished ADAMTS13 activity, and a high inhibitor titer are consistent with iTTP. Although the initial PLASMIC score suggested an intermediate probability of iTTP, therapeutic plasma exchange was not initiated due to a paucity of schistocytes on initial blood smear, and hypertensive emergency was a reasonable explanation for thrombotic microangiopathy. Choice A is incorrect because the hemolysis and altered mental status did not improve with blood pressure control. Rituximab (choice C) is not recommended as monotherapy for iTTP. Platelet transfusion (choice D) is contraindicated in iTTP because it can potentiate microvascular thrombosis and increase mortality. TTP is defined by reduced activity of ADAMTS13, an enzyme that cleaves von Willebrand factor (vWF), and is caused by immune dysfunction (iTTP) or pathogenic variants of theADAMTS13gene (congenital TTP). In iTTP, antibodies neutralize or increase clearance of ADAMTS13, thereby decreasing ADAMTS13 activity. ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% to 20% leads to formation of large vWF multimers, causing microvasculature thromboses, such as myocardial infarction and stroke.1 ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% in patients with thrombocytopenia and MAHA is diagnostic of TTP.1Decreased ADAMTS13 activity (10%-40% activity) without MAHA may occur in pregnancy, uremia, and inflammation (eg, severe sepsis, acute liver failure, multiple sclerosis, COVID-19). MAHA without decreased ADAMTS13 activity may occur with hypertensive emergency, disseminated intravascular coagulation, HELLP syndrome (preeclampsia, hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, low platelet count), hemolytic uremic syndrome, and scleroderma renal crisis.2Obtaining results of ADAMTS13 activity testing typically takes several days. Therefore, the PLASMIC clinical prediction tool can guide decisions about initiating empirical treatment for iTTP. The PLASMIC score includes 7 laboratory values (platelet count, reticulocyte count, haptoglobin level, indirect bilirubin level, mean corpuscular volume, international normalized ratio, creatinine level) and ranges from 0 to 7, with scores 6 to 7 considered as indicating high risk of TTP.3 First-line therapy for iTTP includes therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Rituximab, a monoclonal antibody against CD20, is also recommended to reduce relapse rates,4although randomized trial data are lacking.5Caplacizumab, a humanized, bivalent immunoglobulin fragment, was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2019 for initial treatment of iTTP along with therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Adding caplacizumab to therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids reduces rates of refractory iTTP, exacerbations of iTTP, and treatment response time but does not improve survival.6-8However, caplacizumab is expensive and increases bleeding risk.9 A response to TTP therapy is defined as a platelet count greater than 150 000 cells/μL for 2 consecutive days and LDH level less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, without new or progressive ischemic organ injury.10Clinical remission is defined by absence of thrombocytopenia and hemolysis, clinical stability, and a sustained response for 30 days or longer or ADAMTS13 activity 20% or greater. On hospital day 4, after ADAMTS13 activity result was reported at 6%, the patient was treated with daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg daily) for 3 days, followed by methylprednisolone (65 mg daily) for 3 days, and prednisone (50 mg daily), which was tapered by 10 mg every 3 days. After 5 daily therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, her ADAMTS13 activity was 14% and platelet count was 173 000 cells/μL, and she declined further plasma exchange. Beginning on hospital day 18, the patient received 4 weekly infusions of rituximab (375 mg/m2). On hospital day 30, discharge medications included amlodipine, labetalol, and prednisone (30 mg daily); platelet count was 191 000 cells/μL, and hemoglobin level was 13.2 g/dL. Approximately 1.5 years after initial presentation, the patient appeared well and was not taking iTTP-directed therapy. Platelet count was 220 000 cells/μL and ADAMTS13 activity was 66% without a detectable inhibitor.

1. Mental Demand
   Definition:

   - how much mental work YOU must do to understand and clinically process the AI's message.

   Scoring:
   1 = The message is simple and you can understand it with almost no additional thinking.
       Example: "I agree. The findings you mentioned support your current diagnosis."
   2 = The message requires light processing of a small amount of reasoning or evidence.
       Example: "That seems reasonable. Could you confirm whether the fever began before
       or after the rash?"
   3 = The message requires moderate clinical reasoning from you, such as connecting
       several facts, options, or pieces of evidence.
       Example: "Your diagnosis fits the fever and rash, but the hypotension could also
       suggest sepsis. Can we compare those possibilities briefly?"
   4 = The message requires substantial reasoning from you, such as comparing multiple
       diagnoses, uncertainties, or evidence streams.
       Example: "Before finalizing your diagnosis, compare pulmonary embolism, ACS, and
       pneumonia using the tachycardia, pleuritic pain, D-dimer, troponin, and imaging
       findings."
   5 = The message requires very complex reasoning from you, such as deeply revising your
       differential or holding several competing diagnoses against multiple evidence streams
       at once. This does NOT require a literal "from scratch" rebuild -- being asked to
       compare three or more diagnoses across several findings AND explain how each fits or
       is ruled out already qualifies.
       Example: "Your current diagnosis may not explain the key findings. Compare PE, ACS,
       pneumonia, and aortic dissection: for each, state which evidence supports or rules
       it out, and explain which best fits the overall picture."

2. Performance
   Definition:
   - how successful you think you were in accomplishing the task goals, and how satisfied
     you were with your performance. Performance is anchored from Good to Poor.
   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task
     after the AI's message.
   - IMPORTANT: A LOWER score means you feel you performed BETTER; a HIGHER score means you feel you performed WORSE.

   Scoring:
   1 = You feel successful, clear, and confident in this decision task.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is consistent with the key findings, especially X and Y."
   2 = You feel mostly successful, with only minor uncertainty.
       Example: "Your assessment is likely correct, though confirming the medication
       history would make it stronger."
   3 = You feel moderately uncertain or in need of additional checking.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is plausible, but one finding does not fully fit. We
       should check whether another diagnosis explains it better."
   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.
       Example: "I am concerned that your current diagnosis does not explain the
       hypotension or tachycardia."
   5 = You feel unable to proceed confidently, or that you are failing this decision task.
       Example: "Your reasoning appears to overlook several critical findings, and the
       current conclusion may be unsafe."
   This is NEVER about whether you are objectively right. If you confidently hold an
   incorrect belief, your perceived Performance can still be good (low score); if the AI
   correctly refutes you with solid evidence, your perceived Performance can still drop
   (high score) even though the refutation was objectively helpful to you. Rate only how
   successful and in-control YOU feel, never accuracy.

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.
   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's
     message.

   Scoring:
   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.
       Example: "Agreed. Your choice is consistent with the case."
   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.
       Example: "Can you confirm whether the patient had recent travel?"
   3 = Moderate effort; you must explain, organize, or provide some reasoning.
       Example: "Can you briefly explain why you think pneumonia is more likely than PE?"
   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.
       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and
       pleuritic pain."
   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule
       out several alternatives with explicit evidence. This does NOT require a literal
       "rebuild from scratch" -- being pushed to justify your stance against three or more
       competing options already qualifies.
       Example: "For each of PE, ACS, and pneumonia, explain which evidence supports or
       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."
   Do not confuse this with Mental Demand: "Compare PE, ACS, and pneumonia using the
   evidence" has high Mental Demand (a lot to think through) but if no reply is required of
   you, Effort can stay low -- you only have to read and absorb it. Conversely, "You said PE
   is unlikely. Please justify that." is short and easy to understand (Mental Demand may be
   only moderate) but forces you to actively construct a defense, so Effort is high. Effort
   is about how much active work YOU must produce, not how complex the input was.

4. Frustration
   Definition:
   - how insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, or annoyed you felt, as opposed to
     secure, gratified, content, relaxed, or complacent.
   - how much irritation, stress, pressure, discouragement, or loss of autonomy the AI's
     message imposes on YOU.

   1 = Very low frustration; the message is calm, respectful, and unlikely to pressure you.

   2 = Low frustration; mild discomfort is possible but it remains easy for you to continue.

   3 = Moderate frustration; the AI raises concerns, disagreement, or uncertainty in a

   4 = High frustration; the AI strongly challenges you or may trigger your defensiveness.

   5 = Very high frustration; you may feel undermined, dismissed, attacked, or pressured.

   Frustration is not just "the AI disagreed with me" -- it is about HOW the disagreement is

Although the initial PLASMIC score suggested an intermediate probability of iTTP, therapeutic plasma exchange was not initiated due to a paucity of schistocytes on initial blood smear, and hypertensive emergency was a reasonable explanation for thrombotic microangiopathy. Choice A is incorrect because the hemolysis and altered mental status did not improve with blood pressure control. Rituximab (choice C) is not recommended as monotherapy for iTTP. Platelet transfusion (choice D) is contraindicated in iTTP because it can potentiate microvascular thrombosis and increase mortality. TTP is defined by reduced activity of ADAMTS13, an enzyme that cleaves von Willebrand factor (vWF), and is caused by immune dysfunction (iTTP) or pathogenic variants of theADAMTS13gene (congenital TTP). In iTTP, antibodies neutralize or increase clearance of ADAMTS13, thereby decreasing ADAMTS13 activity. ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% to 20% leads to formation of large vWF multimers, causing microvasculature thromboses, such as myocardial infarction and stroke.1 ADAMTS13 activity less than 10% in patients with thrombocytopenia and MAHA is diagnostic of TTP.1Decreased ADAMTS13 activity (10%-40% activity) without MAHA may occur in pregnancy, uremia, and inflammation (eg, severe sepsis, acute liver failure, multiple sclerosis, COVID-19). MAHA without decreased ADAMTS13 activity may occur with hypertensive emergency, disseminated intravascular coagulation, HELLP syndrome (preeclampsia, hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, low platelet count), hemolytic uremic syndrome, and scleroderma renal crisis.2Obtaining results of ADAMTS13 activity testing typically takes several days. Therefore, the PLASMIC clinical prediction tool can guide decisions about initiating empirical treatment for iTTP. The PLASMIC score includes 7 laboratory values (platelet count, reticulocyte count, haptoglobin level, indirect bilirubin level, mean corpuscular volume, international normalized ratio, creatinine level) and ranges from 0 to 7, with scores 6 to 7 considered as indicating high risk of TTP.3 First-line therapy for iTTP includes therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Rituximab, a monoclonal antibody against CD20, is also recommended to reduce relapse rates,4although randomized trial data are lacking.5Caplacizumab, a humanized, bivalent immunoglobulin fragment, was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2019 for initial treatment of iTTP along with therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids. Adding caplacizumab to therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids reduces rates of refractory iTTP, exacerbations of iTTP, and treatment response time but does not improve survival.6-8However, caplacizumab is expensive and increases bleeding risk.9 A response to TTP therapy is defined as a platelet count greater than 150 000 cells/μL for 2 consecutive days and LDH level less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, without new or progressive ischemic organ injury.10Clinical remission is defined by absence of thrombocytopenia and hemolysis, clinical stability, and a sustained response for 30 days or longer or ADAMTS13 activity 20% or greater. On hospital day 4, after ADAMTS13 activity result was reported at 6%, the patient was treated with daily therapeutic plasma exchange and methylprednisolone (1000 mg daily) for 3 days, followed by methylprednisolone (65 mg daily) for 3 days, and prednisone (50 mg daily), which was tapered by 10 mg every 3 days. After 5 daily therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, her ADAMTS13 activity was 14% and platelet count was 173 000 cells/μL, and she declined further plasma exchange. Beginning on hospital day 18, the patient received 4 weekly infusions of rituximab (375 mg/m2). On hospital day 30, discharge medications included amlodipine, labetalol, and prednisone (30 mg daily); platelet count was 191 000 cells/μL, and hemoglobin level was 13.2 g/dL. Approximately 1.5 years after initial presentation, the patient appeared well and was not taking iTTP-directed therapy. Platelet count was 220 000 cells/μL and ADAMTS13 activity was 66% without a detectable inhibitor.
